JC2023_10-26848-rbgf-v16-6-p3088-3102.reason: Field experiment in Caruaru-PE with identical small boxes (37 x 60 cm). An uncovered reference box was compared with floating PET bottles (reported surface coverage 72.8% and 74.4%), suspended polyethylene screens (14%, 50% and 80% shading) and a suspended Tetrapak sheet. Total evaporation and efficiency are reported per cover for two campaigns, so phi and the control are both available.
JC2023_10-26848-rbgf-v16-6-p3088-3102.same_study_as: Nascimento, J.C. - master's dissertation, UFPE (PPGECAM, Centro Academico do Agreste, Caruaru); the article states it is part of the first author's master's (dissertation title not given)
JC2023_10-26848-rbgf-v16-6-p3088-3102.notes: Site: UFPE Centro Academico do Agreste, Caruaru-PE. The paper calls the climate 'tropical semiarido'; the site is borderline As/BSh and BSh is assigned. Boxes are rectangular, 37 x 60 cm (0.222 m2) and 14 cm high (max 22 L), with about 1 mm freeboard. There is one box per treatment. Evaporation is the water-level drop read with a metal tape at the box centre; covers are partly opened to read. Rain enters the boxes, readings are zero when P >= E, and screens may intercept or wick rain, which explains the negative S of two screens in Campaign 1. Campaign 1 ran Jan-Aug 2020 with 38 readings and staggered starts; the Table 1 totals cover only the period with all six boxes (from the 7th reading, 32 readings), and no dates are given. Campaign 2 ran 29 Aug 2020 - 22 Jan 2021 (20 readings) and added the black 80% screen and the Tetrapak. The Table 3 caption wrongly says 'Etapa 1'; it holds the Campaign 2 totals. For each campaign two analyses are given as separate rows: (a) total evaporation and reported efficiency (Tables 1 and 3), and (b) the mean daily evaporation on intervals with P < 1 mm (Tables 2 and 4, S computed). Both rows describe the same boxes and period, so pick one per condition and do not pool them. Phi: bottle coverage was reported (green 200 mL bottles 0.728, transparent 250 mL bottles 0.744; bottles tied together and ballasted with 95 and 145 mL of water). Screen shading/cover fractions are manufacturer values (mosquito nets 14%; black shade nets 50% for the larger mesh spacing ('# maior'/'maior espessura') and 80% for the smaller one). Tetrapak phi of 1 is inferred from 'blocks all incident solar energy'. The Tetrapak degraded quickly; the bottles aged between campaigns. The reference box measured 1908 mm from 10 Jan 2020 to 22 Jan 2021 (Table 5). The Quadro 2 literature values (Saraiva 2001, Alvarez 2006, Simon 2016, Han 2020, etc.) are cited data and were not extracted.

do2021_evapora-o-em-pequenos-reservat-ri.reason: Measured tank experiment at UFPE Caruaru. Floating PET-bottle covers with computed coverage (72.8% and 74.4%), suspended polyethylene screens and a tetrapak sheet were each compared with an identical uncovered tank. Total evaporation and % reduction are tabulated for two stages (Tables 2 and 4).
do2021_evapora-o-em-pequenos-reservat-ri.notes: MSc thesis, Nascimento 2021 (UFPE). Tanks are plastic mortar boxes, 0.60 x 0.37 m (2220 cm2 per the manufacturer; Melo 2023 gives 0.56 x 0.37 m), 0.14 m high, 22 L. Weekly manual tape readings at the tank centre, with water topped up. Precipitation was NOT subtracted (pp.58-59): the open tank catches all rain and the screens may intercept it, which explains the negative efficiencies of the screens in Stage 1. Stage 1 ran 10 Jan to 29 Aug 2020 (p.57). Its totals start at the 7th reading (32 readings), so the exact period is not given. Stage 2 ran 29 Aug 2020 to 22 Jan 2021 with 20 weekly readings, hot and dry; the screens were replaced with new identical ones and the bottles were not replaced. Bottle phi was computed by the author from the projected bottle areas (24 green bottles x 67.33 cm2; 20 clear x 82.63 cm2) over 2220 cm2 (eqs 2-7, pp.40-41) and is called an approximation. Screen phi is the nominal cover/shade fraction: mosquito mesh 14% (reseller, p.36), black shade net 50% (larger mesh) and 80% (smaller mesh, manufacturer, pp.37-38). The p.66 text calls the smaller mesh '70% de cobertura', which is inconsistent. The tetrapak was a non-porous suspended sheet meant to block all sunlight (p.42); it degraded quickly. Tables 3 and 5 give precipitation-free estimates: mean daily evaporation on days with rain < 1 mm. These are recorded in the row notes and not as separate rows, to avoid double counting. Continued with new data (Jan 2021 to Dec 2022 and a 500 L phase) by Melo 2023 (de2023_...) on the same installation.

de2023_t-cnicas-de-redu-o-da-evapora-o-e.reason: Measured tank experiment with floating PET bottles and suspended screens or tetrapak against an uncovered reference tank. It covers 2 years (Phase 1, small boxes) plus a 500 L Phase 2. Total and seasonal evaporation and % reduction are tabulated.
de2023_t-cnicas-de-redu-o-da-evapora-o-e.notes: MSc thesis, Melo 2023 (UFPE). Phase 1 continues the Nascimento 2021 installation at UFPE/CAA Caruaru with new data: 22 Jan 2021 to 30 Dec 2022, 61 weekly readings. It is the same installation, so same_study_as is filled, but it is not a duplicate. Phase 1 boxes measure 0.37 x 0.56 x 0.13 m (p.51). Phase 2 (IPA Caruaru, 17 Mar to 22 Jun 2023, rainy season, 8 fortnightly readings) used buried 500 L polyethylene tanks: rim diameter 1.22 m, base 0.95 m, depth 0.58 m. Phase 2 covers were TPG, clear PET with 125 mL water, and tetrapak. EVAPORATION METHOD (pp.58-59): Eq. 25 subtracts P, but the author states that precipitation was NOT taken into account, and negative net values (rain gains) were set to zero. Screens partly intercept rain and the tetrapak-covered tank receives none, which biases comparisons in rainy periods. PET phi is not restated here; the values come from Nascimento 2021 (green 0.728, clear 0.744). Melo swaps the bottle volumes (green 250 mL, clear 200 mL; 95 and 145 mL of water). Screens: TPP = small aperture (80% shading), TPG = large aperture (50%), TV/TB = mosquito mesh (14%); phi = nominal shade fraction. Tetrapak covers were frequently replaced, while the PET bottles aged (became opaque and deformed). Seasonal rows (Tables 9-12, 53, 64, 75) are given for the PET bottles only, to stay within the row limit. Tetrapak was the best cover in every season (29-66%). Monthly values for all covers are in Table 8.
